newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - ADRS ease in N.Y. on dollar worries.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - ADRS ease in N.Y. on dollar worries.

text.p: Foreign shares in New York were largely flat on Thursday, with Fila Holdings up sharply on improved earnings, traders and analysts said.
Most American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) were weighed by lower overseas markets stemming from a weaker dollar.
"Most overseas markets are down. There was no real rally from yesterday's rally on Wall Street," said Andrew Melinek, head of ADR research and sales with NatWest Securities.

Fila, an Italian clothing and footwear group, rose 6-3/8, or more than eight percent, to 82 after it reported third-quarter earnings per share of 491 lire against 294 for the same period a year before.
Royal Dutch Petroleum Co's ADRs rose 1/8 to 160-5/8 following an announcement that its Shell Oil Co unit and Mobil Corp would merge their California exploration and production businesses.
Swedish auto maker Scania fell one point to 25-3/8 after it reported nine-month earnings below expectations.
Shares in British Airways rose 1-3/8 to 93-1/4 on news NatWest Securities and ABN AMRO Hoare Govett repeated their positive views of the stock.
Gucci Group N.V. was up 1-5/8 to 76 after Merrill Lynch named its shares a global focus stock.
Latin American shares were quiet, with analysts waiting for the Mexican government to present its budget later in the day.
There were 196 advancers and 248 decliners among 807 ADRs in late-morning trade. Volume was 28.5 million shares.
